html: The Ikoots, better known as the Huave, are an Indigenous people of the lagoons on the Pacific coast of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in Oaxaca, Mexico. Their language is an isolate. They live in towns such as San Mateo del Mar and San Francisco del Mar on narrow sand bars between lagoon and sea, and live mainly by fishing and shrimping. A colonial account says they came by sea from the south. The Zapotec, who moved into the Isthmus in the 1400s, took much of their land and pushed them onto the coast. A large wind farm planned on their lagoon in the 2010s was dropped after strong local opposition. Their neighbours inland include the Mixe.
